narrator.instruct: Gripping, energetic storyteller telling a true, surprising invention story with wonder, brisk, excited and punchy, never calm.

benedictus.instruct: A young chemist late at night, suddenly remembering something important, jumping up from his chair, breathless and thrilled, quick.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A glass flask shattered on a hard floor, and then it simply refused to fall apart.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Paris, nineteen oh three: the lab of the chemist and artist Édouard Bénédictus.
lines.say: Paris, nineteen oh three: the lab of the chemist and artist, Ay-dwar Bay-nay-deek-tooss.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He expected a mess of splinters. But the flask had cracked into a web, and kept its shape.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Inside, it had held collodion, a liquid plastic, which dried into a clear film that held every shard.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He set it aside, and forgot all about it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then Paris filled with motor cars, and the cars began to crash.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The story goes that he read about a crash where people were cut by flying glass.

lines.speaker: benedictus
lines.text: That old flask, it held together!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And as the story is told, he worked all night on a new kind of glass.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You see, he made a sandwich: glass, a thin layer of plastic, then glass again. When it breaks, the shards stick to the plastic.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He patented it in nineteen oh nine. But car makers were slow to want it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So its first big job was in the First World War: the eyepieces of gas masks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then it went into car windshields, and it is still there today.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So when a stone hits your windshield, it cracks like that flask, and holds.
